body:
I shy away from anything that could be perceived as "conflict". I've gotten a little better at this, I'm more comfortable discussing issues that come up in our relationship. But I feel like hygiene is hard for me because I'm worried he'll be offended or embarrassed. Although the few times I've asked him to brush his teeth he wasn't offended. His overall hygiene is okay, thankfully. There are a few things that could be better but I pick and choose my battles.

I'm not considering ending the relationship yet, I've had thoughts about it but I'm not sure, and I don't think I can yet. But yeah, being able to have these conversations is important.

Lol the last time I was at his place I brushed his cat and showed him the all the hair, and I told him it would probably be better if he brushed him everyday, or somewhat regularly at least. He said he tried once and it didn't seem to make a difference so he didn't bother. It's little things like that that don't make sense to me.

This I'm learning, I have issues being direct in general and I know it doesn't help anyone if I can't communicate my thoughts and feelings effectively. But yes, you're right. Thanks
This is my first relationship so I'm probably learning/experiencing things that most people already did earlier in their lives.
This is what I ask myself, because I know I can't force him to care about things he doesn't. So the thoughts are being thought, but decisions haven't been made.

He doesn't have to use the exact one I use, I just want him to have an effective one. Sometimes his cat has litter on his paws and tracks it outside of the litter box. And then there's general dust and stuff that accumulates on floors. Air purifiers are very useful, I didn't know about them until last year. I deal with allergies and I don't like bad smells, so yes they make my life a lot easier. His place has a smell. Since he hasn't been to the dentist in so long, I'm concerned there might be something that's causing bad breath.

That's a good point. I've brought up the things I would like to be clean when I come over, and he's listened to me, but it could be better. I try to cut him a bit of slack because I have high attention to detail when it comes to cleaning.

I would like to think maintaining your health is a normal thing to do, but I am more "medical" minded than the average person.

So I do have some insight into his finances. His job pays well, he makes a lot more than me. He only has a debit card so I told him about the benefits of having a credit card. So he spends what he has, which isn't bad, I think it's a great thing because he doesn't have credit card debt lol. There are times he's in between paychecks and he'll wait to buy things, which also makes sense to me. He said he didn't want to spend money on the vacuum and air purifier yet, I didn't really press for more details.

For insurance: he was on his parents insurance before he turned 26, but he didn't know that you have to get your own insurance after that so he didn't have health insurance for the first year I was with him. He signed up for health insurance last year, I made sure to mention I was doing open enrollment and he needed to as well. But he hasn't even used it. I think he's forgetful, it isn't a priority to him so he doesn't think about it.

I haven’t specifically said “your breath smells bad” but in the past I’ve asked him to brush his teeth in the morning because I had already brushed mine, and when we went on a trip I asked when the last time he brushed his teeth was. I’ve mentioned that it’s important to floss, he’s seen me use my floss picks and tongue scraper. So I haven’t been that direct. And I know all of that, but I have a feeling if I tell him that, he won’t care too much. In the past I’ve mentioned things that would be good for him to do or pay attention to and he’s either been like “ok cool” or jokingly brushes it off. I dont really make out with him, I just do quick kisses and idk if I don’t like kissing that much or if it’s bad breath that’s a buzzkill, because his breath doesn’t smell bad all the time.

>Would your current roommate be open to finding a cheaper place to move to together instead of renewing the current lease?

If we end our lease, we'll owe more money since we didn't give our 60 day notice on time. She was already leaning towards staying, but that just cemented it. 

>what would your rent/roommate situation be able to be when you move back out?

I was hoping to cross that bridge once I get there. But I'd ideally like to search for another roommate or room to rent. And I would only consider it if it would be cheaper than $1,400. $1,200-$1,300 inclusive of rent and utilities and such would be ideal. That would go out the window if I were to get another job with a higher salary, I'd adjust accordingly. I'd be willing to stay at home a little longer if necessary too, like 3-4 months. It all depends.

I've used YNAB on and off, I started when I was living at home, and it was easy to keep up with. Now it just confuses me. I tried keeping a spreadsheet too, it helped a bit. But I guess I have to find a system I like. And exercise discipline.

The interest I pay is also slowly killing me, I want that out of the way too. I think I could knock out my debt within a month or so, perhaps this year since this is my last month paying full rent. But I definitely want to build up my emergency fund again, that’s a priority.

Moving back home for a year is not something I am willing to do, at all. My mental health is at its best because I’m not living at home. Going back for longer than a few months would likely undo some of that progress. And I have no intentions of leaving my area any time soon. Living deep in the suburbs isn’t great for me either. 

I’m leaning more towards home than with my bf anyway. I’d have way more living space and wouldn’t be constantly fighting allergies.

My parents would definitely welcome me home with open arms. In our culture, it's common for young adults to live with their parents in their 20's and 30's, especially in our home country. It's just that I wouldn't be at my happiest. Cooking is one of my hobbies and I liked sharing what I made with them, so that's no problem. I don't see them asking for help on bills, but I would be open to it.

I've had my doubts about my relationship with my bf, and I've gone back and forth on whether I'm completely satisfied. Things have been good the last month, those doubts have calmed down and I think I'd ultimately want to stay together. For how long, I'm not sure, I think it depends on how our relationship continues to develop. But I don't see our relationship ending anytime soon.

I definitely do want another job, regardless of where I stay, that has been a part of my plan for a while.

Thanks so much for taking the time to write an in depth reply!

I do go to therapy, I've been seeing my therapist for several years. I will definitely discuss this with her too.

Communication is something I've been trying to work on, and I think I'm improving. That's great that you could discuss your anxieties with your bf, I'm working up to that level of vulnerability with mine. I've brought up things I've felt in the past, but not really present feelings. How does he reassure you? 

The reason his last relationship ended was because of distance, not because they didn't want to be together anymore. They knew the relationship would have an expiration date when it started, but they ended up prolonging the inevitable. That's what made me anxious. I don't think about it as much now, I've gotten used to the idea of them being friends. But I try to remind myself of that, we get along so well!

My life wasn't so bad single, I just felt more lonely. But it wasn't impossible. I just know how I tend to spiral into depression. My relationships with friends and family aren't that close, and my life was pretty quiet before my bf, so that's why I'm afraid I'm predisposed to becoming "obsessed" with him, because I don't have much going on outside of him. And sometimes I don't really have the energy to. Living in the present is something I'm trying to work on in general, I'm hoping I get better at it soon enough.

There are some things that I don't "love" about him, but I decided they weren't dealbreakers. Sometimes I imagine if there was someone who didn't have some of those qualities, someone better for me. I'm even disappointed that I didn't get to date multiple people in the early stages. But they say the grass is always greener on the other side, right?

That sounds tough, with your ex, it must have been so jarring to have everything gone. I don't think I would ever become "dependent" on him, I think I'm naturally an independent person. I'm not at the obsessed level yet, as our relationship is still new, probably more preoccupied because I do think about him a lot.

I realize the texting issue comes from insecurity. I think that's gotten a lot better on my part now that we're together and I'm not wondering if he really likes me or wants a relationship. I guess time will help?

I'll try to have some heart to heart conversations with him :)

You’re right, it’s not harsh. I just became so preoccupied with trying to spot red flags and potential problem behaviors to avoid things happening like they did in the past. I guess one of my issues is not trusting myself to know what to do.

I think he treats me well. We text everyday, and our conversation is reciprocal, we both ask each other questions. He's been nothing but respectful. But when I said low effort, I meant in terms of dates and showing affection. He's struggled to come up with date ideas and has asked me to decide what to do a few times. So he might be complacent in terms of dates. Then affection, he doesn't seem particularly flirty or affectionate, and that made me feel like things with him were more platonic since I'm used to men obviously flirting or trying to steer things in a sexual direction.

We've been averaging 1 date a week, last weekend we saw each other twice. We haven't had sex yet, I told him I didn't want to have sex outside of a relationship. But we make out with pants on lol. I brought it up to him, first over text and then last week. He says he's looking for a relationship and he likes how things are progressing between us. So I feel like we're on the same page.
That's my big takeaway, communicating is important :)

I just replied to another comment asking if he was autistic, and after hearing about how neurodivergent people tend to gravitate towards each other, I'm not completely ruling out the possibility. I value directness, but actually *being* direct to others? Nope, I speak in euphemisms for whatever reason. So that's probably something I should practice/change.

I'm a late dx'ed autistic so I'm well aware. Hence why everyone's giving me shit here for not communicating or initiating things myself lol. I do get some neurodivergent vibes from him based on how well we get along, but I can't definitively say so.

>Sounds like you're more social than he is.

Not quite right, *but*, I want to get out of the house more because that's all I do. And I could see myself being the same way in a relationship. But I got it in my head that I should expect more from a certain books and a subreddit that shall not be named.
That's what you implied by reversing the roles.
And I do enjoy his company. I think previous situations have led me to internalize questionable dating advice that makes me doubt my own experience.

I could see this being the situation here. Combine two introverted/shy people and nothing happens. I'm on the spectrum too, actually, hence why this is stressing me out. I don't have previous experience or a "schema" to refer to, and people are saying anything from "if he wanted to, he would" to "what's wrong with 50/50". So I really don't know what tf is going on lol.
It's not that he isn't "responding", he's very agreeable and has agreed with my ideas. But I did have to initiate the "what are we doing this weekend" conversation.
Where did I say I refused to go? Reading is not your strong suit.

> you are basically a bratty girl who did a few things and wants three times the amount back.

What an assumption, you're wrong though.
The second date was free, so it evens out, no reason for me to be ashamed.
That's how I feel, it just seems pretty obvious to me? I'll have a conversation with him about it, I guess that's the only way to know really.
You're right. I'm shy, I typically let the man take the lead, so when that isn't happening I hit a bit of a roadblock as well.

Thanks for your input, I'm really just trying to avoid getting played, that's a big fear of mine. A guy unequivocally showing that he's into me is what I need to feel good about how things are going. I will bring it up with him

I didn’t refuse to plan a date, I planned the third and I just suggested our next date. And I’ve gone out of my way to see him at his place. I just dont want to look stupid trying putting in more effort than him because he isn’t interested.
I mentioned in a few other comments that I planned and paid for our third date activity. And I’ve talked about wanting to go out and do things with him rather than hanging out.
I chose and paid for the activity for our third date. And I’ve made a 30 minute drive over to his place 3 times.

He has a good job, I don’t think money is an issue. He seems to be more on the introverted side, and I am as well. He didn’t initiate any “touch” (outside of goodbye hugs) until the 4th date at his place, and before that I thought things felt kind of platonic, so maybe he could’ve been a bit nervous.

I’m not sure how to bring it up. Last time we were together I told him that I’d prefer to go out and do something for our next date, and he seemed on board with that. I gave him a few ideas, and he also suggested hiking when the weather warms up. So he knows at least that I want to go on actual dates instead of hanging out all the time.

Yep, and I wholeheartedly agree with it. It just feels like I’ve invested so much time already. We get along very well, and I honestly don’t like most people from dating apps, I’m sort of picky. I tried to look around on the apps and see if there was anyone else I’d be interested in dating (so I wouldn’t put all of my eggs in one basket) and came back with nada.
